title: Hello, explorer!
explain: Python is a language for giving computers instructions. print() displays a message. Put words inside matching quotation marks.
mission: Print Hello, explorer! on its own line.
hint: Change the words between the quotation marks.

title: A tiny postcard
explain: Python runs instructions from top to bottom. Each print() starts a new line.
mission: Print My name is Python on the first line and Let’s explore! on the second. Use a straight apostrophe in Let's.
hint: Use double quotes around a message containing an apostrophe.
solution:
print("My name is Python")
print("Let's explore!")
expected:
My name is Python
Let's explore!

title: Pocket calculator
explain: Use + to add, - to subtract, * to multiply, and / to divide. Numbers do not need quotation marks.
mission: Print the result of 7 multiplied by 8.

title: Secret notes
explain: A comment starts with #. Python ignores it. Comments explain your ideas to future you.
mission: Keep a comment in your code, then print Ready for adventure!
solution:
# My adventure starts here
print("Ready for adventure!")

title: Launch countdown
explain: Mix text and numbers in separate print statements to build a little rocket launch sequence.
mission: Print 3, 2, 1, and Liftoff! on four separate lines.

title: Name your explorer
explain: A variable is a name for a value. name = "Pip" stores text. print(name) displays it.
mission: Set name to Pip and print name.

title: Treasure pouch
explain: Variables can hold numbers. coins = coins + 5 updates your coins using the old value.
mission: Start with 10 coins, add 5 to coins, then print coins.

title: Say it your way
explain: An f-string inserts a variable into text: f"Hi, {name}!". The f before the opening quote matters.
mission: Use name in an f-string to print Hello, Pip!

title: Sharing snacks
explain: // divides and rounds down. % gives the remainder. For example, 7 % 3 is 1.
mission: Print how many snacks each friend gets (4), then how many are left (1). Use // and %.
hint: Print snacks // friends, then snacks % friends.
solution:
snacks = 17
friends = 4
print(snacks // friends)
print(snacks % friends)

title: Explorer ID
explain: Combine variables and f-strings to make a character card. You can use more than one variable in an f-string.
mission: Print Explorer: Pip and Level: 1 on separate lines using the variables.
hint: Use print(f"Explorer: {name}") and another f-string for level.

title: The forest gate
explain: An if runs code only when a condition is true. End the if line with a colon and indent its instructions with four spaces.
mission: If coins is at least 10, print Gate open!.
starter:
coins = 12
if coins >= 10:
    # Write your message here
    pass

title: Rain or shine
explain: else: provides an alternative when the if condition is false. True and False are Python’s boolean values.
mission: Use the else branch to print Bring a hat.
hint: Replace pass with a print statement.

title: Three secret doors
explain: elif checks another condition after an if is false. Python uses == to compare two values; = stores a value.
mission: For door 2, print A treasure chest.
hint: Add elif door == 2: with an indented print.
starter:
door = 2
if door == 1:
    print("A sleepy dragon")
# Add an elif for door 2

title: Both keys
explain: and needs both conditions to be true. or needs at least one. Use these to make smarter decisions.
mission: If has_map and has_key are both true, print Adventure unlocked!.
solution:
has_map = True
has_key = True
if has_map and has_key:
    print("Adventure unlocked!")

title: Treasure judge
explain: Write a reward system. Check the biggest reward first so a score of 90 does not get the lower reward.
mission: Use if / elif / else to print Gold for 80+, Silver for 50–79, and Bronze otherwise. We check three scores.
hint: Start with if score >= 80:, then elif score >= 50:.
starter:
score = 85
# 80 or more: Gold
# 50 or more: Silver
# Otherwise: Bronze

title: Echo meadow
explain: A for loop repeats code. range(3) gives 0, 1, 2: three turns. Indent the code you want to repeat.
mission: Print Hello! three times using a for loop.

title: Stepping stones
explain: range(1, 6) starts at 1 and stops before 6. The loop variable holds each number in turn.
mission: Use a for loop to print 1 through 5, each on its own line.

title: Backpack inventory
explain: A list stores several items in square brackets. A loop can visit each item: for item in backpack:.
mission: Loop through backpack and print each item on a separate line.
hint: Write for item in backpack: and indent print(item).

title: A reusable spell
explain: A function packages instructions under a name. Define one with def cheer():, then call it with cheer().
mission: Define cheer() to print You can do this!, then call it twice.
hint: Put print in the function, then write cheer() on two lines outside it.
starter:
def cheer():
    # Give your explorer a boost
    pass

# Call your function below
solution:
def cheer():
    print("You can do this!")

cheer()
cheer()
expected:
You can do this!
You can do this!

title: The final campfire
explain: Bring it all together: a list, a loop, a function, and an f-string. Each skill is a tool you can now use to make your own projects.
mission: Define welcome(name) to print Welcome, NAME! and loop through explorers to welcome all three in order.
hint: Inside the function use print(f"Welcome, {name}!"). Then loop through explorers and call welcome(explorer).
starter:
explorers = ["Pip", "Nova", "Ash"]

def welcome(name):
    # Print a welcome using name
    pass

# Welcome each explorer with a loop
expected:
Welcome, Pip!
Welcome, Nova!
Welcome, Ash!

title: A character dictionary
explain: A dictionary stores values under keys. For example, hero = {"name": "Pip"}. Use hero["name"] to read a value.
mission: Create hero with name Pip and level 1. Print the name, then the level on separate lines.
starter:
hero = {}
# Read the name and level

title: Level up
explain: Change a dictionary value by assigning to a key: hero["level"] = 2.
mission: Start with a hero dictionary containing level 1. Update level to 2 and print it.
hint: Read the old level and add 1.

title: A missing key
explain: dictionary.get(key, default) returns a fallback when a key does not exist. This helps avoid KeyError.
mission: Create a hero dictionary without a pet key. Use get() to print No pet yet as a default.

title: Inventory report
explain: Loop through dictionary.items() to get each key and value together: for item, count in bag.items():.
mission: Loop through bag and print map: 1, then snack: 3, each on its own line.

title: Your explorer registry
explain: A list can contain dictionaries. A function can accept a dictionary as its parameter. Combine these tools for a little registry.
mission: Define introduce(hero). Loop through heroes and call introduce to print Pip is level 1, then Nova is level 2.
hint: In introduce use print(f"{hero['name']} is level {hero['level']}").
starter:
heroes = [{"name": "Pip", "level": 1}, {"name": "Nova", "level": 2}]

def introduce(hero):
    pass

# Introduce each hero
expected:
Pip is level 1
Nova is level 2
